transcript.text:
If your washing machine won’t spin, try these safe checks:

1. Pause and unplug it before touching anything.
2. Check the load: A single heavy item or overloaded drum can stop spinning. Remove some items and spread the rest evenly.
3. Make sure it drained: If there is water left in the drum, it often will not spin. Check/clean the drain filter (usually behind a small flap at the bottom front) and make sure the drain hose isn’t kinked or blocked. Have towels ready—water may come out.
4. Close the door firmly: The door/lid lock must engage. Look for anything caught in the seal or latch.
5. Check it is level: If it rocks or bangs, adjust the feet so all four sit firmly on the floor.
6. Try a “Drain & Spin” or “Spin” cycle with the drum empty or with a small balanced load.
7. Reset it: Unplug for 5–10 minutes, then reconnect and retry.

If it fills and washes but never spins, common causes are a blocked pump/filter, faulty lid/door lock, worn drive belt, or motor/control fault. If you smell burning, hear grinding, or the drum won’t turn by hand, stop using it and arrange repair.

Tell me:
• Is there water still inside?
• Does it make a humming/clicking/noise?
• Front loader or top loader?
• Brand/model or any error code?

no water left in the drum, its empty. drum sloshes bk n forth n tries to speed up then slows down, no grinding. its a hotpoint with a door on the front, no error code. model on the door label is NSWM 1043C W UK N

That sounds like it is getting through the balance-check phase (rocking the drum back and forth) but not committing to full spin. An empty machine should still spin, so it is not just an uneven load.

Try this once:

1. Turn the machine off and unplug it for 10 minutes.
2. Check the drain-pump filter behind the lower front flap/plinth. Even with no water in the drum, fluff or a small object in the filter can affect the machine’s drain/pressure sensing. Put towels down first.
3. Confirm the drain hose is not squashed/kinked behind the machine.
4. Make sure the washer is stable and not rocking; adjust the front feet if needed.
5. Plug it back in and select Spin & Drain / Drain + Spin, with the spin speed set to the highest available setting — not “0”, “No Spin”, or “Rinse Hold.” Run it empty.

Also listen for a firm door-lock click shortly after starting. If it keeps rocking slowly, tries to speed up, then gives up with no error, likely causes include:

• door-lock issue
• motor speed sensor/motor fault
• wiring or control-board fault
• pressure sensor incorrectly thinking water remains

A blocked filter is the easy DIY possibility; beyond that, don’t remove the back or work on it while powered. If it has always done this since installation, check that the transport bolts were removed from the back—though they usually cause severe banging rather than failure to spin.

For a Hotpoint NSWM 1043C W UK N, if the filter/hose/reset do not change it, it likely needs an appliance engineer. If it is in warranty, use Hotpoint/Whirlpool service rather than an independent repairer.
it doesnt rock, sits steady. spin is on 1000 not no spin. do i really have to do the filter bit? dont really want to unless its needed

No — based on what you’ve described, you do not need to check the filter first. Since the drum is empty and there’s no water left, a blocked filter is less likely.

It sounds more like the machine is trying to begin the spin, then deciding not to continue. Do these easier checks first:

1. Try Spin & Drain with 1–2 dry bath towels inside
   Some machines behave oddly with a completely empty drum during their balance check. Don’t overload it; just use a small, evenly placed load.

2. Listen for the door lock
   Start the cycle and listen for a distinct click from the door area. The door should stay locked throughout. A weak/intermittent lock can let it tumble but prevent a high-speed spin.

3. Turn the drum by hand while switched off
   It should rotate smoothly with mild resistance, without scraping, tight spots, or excessive wobble.

4. Watch the time remaining
   On Spin & Drain, does the time count down normally while it keeps trying, or does it stay stuck at the same number?
• Counts down but never properly spins: more likely motor speed sensing/control issue.
• Stays stuck while repeatedly trying: it may be failing a safety/balance/door-lock check.

If it does the same thing with towels and no error code appears, the filter is worth checking eventually, but it is unlikely to be the main cause. More likely candidates are the door interlock, motor/tacho speed sensor, wiring, or control board—usually an engineer job.
ok i tried it with the mat n a couple of towels in and it spun up fine this time. the mat came out damp not dripping. not sure bout the door click or the time thing tho

That’s a good sign: the washer, motor, door lock, and spin function are probably working.

The damp-but-not-dripping mat suggests it did a proper spin. You don’t need to worry about the door click or timer now, and you don’t need to check the filter unless the problem returns.

It was likely reacting to the completely empty drum / its balance detection. The towels gave it enough weight and movement to complete the spin check.

Next time, just use it normally. A couple of notes:

• Don’t judge it only by an empty Spin & Drain test — try a normal wash load too.
• Bath mats can sometimes become very heavy and unbalanced when wet, so wash them with a couple of towels rather than alone.
• If it starts failing to spin with ordinary, evenly distributed loads, or leaves laundry soaking wet, then it is worth checking the filter and considering a repair.

For now, it sounds like it’s okay.
